chapter_theme: Knowing the Lord's foot and head: the foot is his grace, which shows the soul knowledge, and in the body foot and head lie at the root and the crown. The poet tells how Nandi's feet came onto his head, cut his bonds and took him, and how the Lord, like a parent, deals with each soul by its ripeness.
structure_note: Two verses define foot and head (2425, 2426); the rest speak in the first person of the feet placed on the head (2427, 2429, 2433), in the heart (2428, 2431), and in the body's lotus (2432), and end on the Lord's care for each soul (2434).

2425.reading: The wretched do not know foot and head: the foot is Shakti, grace and the cause, the head is knowledge, and when the foot shows the soul that knowledge, release comes.
2425.nuance: The equation of the foot with Shakti as grace is stated; பாலொன்று ஞானமே பண்பார் தலைஉயிர் is hard to divide, and may make the soul the head, or place it under knowledge. கலதிகள் (the wretched, the ill-fated) is sharp.

2426.reading: People do not know what head and foot are; in the body they are at the crown and at the root, and those who know the knowledge that is head and foot remain as head and foot themselves.
2426.nuance: உச்சி (crown) and மூலம் (root) are taken in the yogic sense as the top of the head and the lowest centre; தலைஅடி can also mean the foot placed on the head, as in 2427. The last line says the knower becomes what he knows.

2427.reading: Nandi, who stood so that the whole earth and the cosmos rose up, so that the strong-footed asuras and the gods were saved, and who afterwards created the world: his pair of feet came upon my head.
2427.nuance: நின்றான் ... மேலுற may recall Siva standing as the column whose head and foot Brahma and Vishnu could not find, which fits a chapter on head and foot; the verse does not name the story. The feet on the head are traditionally the guru's initiation by the feet (திருவடி தீட்சை).

2428.reading: My father's holy feet are within my mind, and my mind is beneath my father's holy feet; if my father cannot know me, I cannot know my father either.
2428.nuance: Lines 1 and 2 reverse each other: the feet in the mind and the mind under the feet. The last two lines make the soul's knowing of the Lord depend on his knowing it first. Sengalvaraya notes a close parallel in Appar's Tevaram (5.91.8).

2429.reading: Beyond the unspoken light of the world and beyond that, where my Lord consented to dwell, he told me the light that cannot be thought and the mantra that cannot be spoken, and I stand wearing his anklet feet.
2429.nuance: உரைசெய்யா மந்திரம் is a mantra not spoken aloud or one beyond speech, yet he 'told' it: the verse holds the paradox of teaching the unsayable. சூடி, wearing as a garland, is the feet on the head again.

2430.reading: Set in yourselves the feet that reveal the Lord, make your understanding steady and recite the flower-feet, and see the times when the one with the river in his matted hair and the woman as his half grants the goal.
2430.nuance: மதியது செய்து may be 'use your understanding' or, in the yogic sense, 'make the moon', the inner lunar breath. கதிசெயும் காலங்கள் (times he grants the goal) is unexplained.

2431.reading: The one who sustains stood with his feet in my heart; the lord of the gods' city stood sustaining; he stood scorching the minds of those who do not think of him, and he stood bearing souls according to their ripeness.
2431.nuance: பரிபாகம் is the soul's ripeness, a Siddhanta term for readiness to receive grace. கரித்து may be 'burning, blackening' or 'witnessing'; its sense against those who do not think of him is unclear. அமராபதி நாதன் uses the name of Indra's city for Siva as lord over the gods.

2432.reading: There is one lotus with three bright flowers, and one's father's feet, two, are in the body; for those who can heat it well and bring it to the right state, it is possible to go today and reach the Lord.
2432.nuance: காய்ச்சிப் பதஞ்செய is a cooking image, boiling down to the right consistency, taken as yogic heat or the ripening of the soul; பதம் also means foot and state. The lotus and its three flowers are not identified; tradition reads them as centres of the yogic body.

2433.reading: He set his foot on my head so that my bonds were cut and cut, so that the confusion of my bewildered heart's delusion was cut, and he sought to take me, who was his portion; what my state became after he took me cannot be told.
2433.nuance: கட்டறக் கட்டற doubles the cutting of bonds. பால்கொண்ட என்னை may be 'me, who belonged to his side' or 'me, who had taken a side'. The verse ends in the ineffable (விளம்ப ஒண்ணாதே).

2434.reading: Like a parent who has seen both the tendencies and the faults of the sons he begot, the Lord who holds to souls deals with each by its nature, doing without anger what fits.
2434.nuance: நாற்றம் is usually smell; here perhaps disposition, or நாற்று (seedling) as what has been raised. குணங்குறை செய்ய (to make up for virtues and lacks) and the third line are loosely built. The point that the Lord's dealings are without hatred (செற்றமிலா) is clear.

links.note: Both join the Lord's feet to the head. The Kural calls a head that does not bow to them useless; in Tirumular the feet come down onto the head, as grace given rather than worship offered.
2427 says Nandi's feet came onto the poet's head; 2433 says what they did there: cut his bonds and his delusion and took him.
2421 makes grace the means to reach the Lord's feet; 2425 makes the feet themselves grace, which shows the soul knowledge.

source_issues: 2425: line 4 reads ஞானத்கைக், a misprint for ஞானத்தைக்.
2433: line 3 reads என்ணைப், a misprint for என்னைப்.
